title: Dakgalbi
subtitle: korean spicy stir-fried chicken
excerpt: Dakgalbi is a Korean stir-fry of marinated chicken, courgette, and spring onion cooked in a sweet and spicy gochujang sauce. It is a fast, one-pan dish with bold flavour. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Dakgalbi originated in Chuncheon, a city in Gangwon Province, Korea, in the 1960s. It became so popular that the area has an entire street dedicated to the dish.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Marinate the chicken up to 12 hours ahead and keep refrigerated.

items.prepNote: boneless, skinless, cut into 3 cm pieces

content.text: Mix all the marinade ingredients together. Add the chicken pieces, toss well, cover, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large frying pan over high heat. Add the marinated chicken and cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes.
Add the onion and carrot. Stir-fry for 3 minutes. Add the courgette and cook for a further 3 minutes.
Reduce the heat to medium. Continue cooking, stirring, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has reduced and clings to everything, about 5 more minutes.
Scatter spring onion over the top and drizzle with sesame oil. Scatter sesame seeds if liked. Serve straight from the wok with steamed rice.

attrs.issue: Sauce is burning before the chicken is cooked
attrs.fix: Lower the heat to medium and add 2 to 3 tablespoons of water to the pan. The gochujang paste can catch on high heat with extended cooking.
Use thigh meat rather than breast. Thigh stays juicy during stir-frying. Do not overcook once the sauce has reduced.
Reduce the gochujang to 2 tablespoons and add an extra teaspoon of sugar. Serving with plenty of steamed rice also helps balance the heat.

content.text: Dakgalbi comes from Chuncheon in the mountains east of Seoul. The city has dozens of restaurants serving it on iron plates at the table. Diners cook the chicken themselves and add rice or noodles towards the end. The leftover sauce and any sticking bits from the pan are fried with rice at the end of the meal.
